meta.census_parts: brain/reader, gobbler/reader-ext, demiurge/reader-ext-dm, dynasty/reader-ext-dl, manifold/manifold-reader-ext, drift/drift-ext

Analyser.note: the data outputs are only fed while the node is active and a Web Audio context exists; nothing is wired into the analyser yet (the Sound children of this node come with the rest of the Sound group); minDecibels, maxDecibels and smoothingTimeConstant go to the audio node when it is made; changing them while it runs is not applied until the next start

Anchor.note: only a #Viewpoint url is followed in the test; any other url goes to body.opts.onAnchor, a page without a handler gets a note and stays where it is (X_ITE 16.6.0 loads the url itself: the bridge never loads a world, that is the host's job); javascript: urls are refused on purpose; target= in parameter is passed to onAnchor, not acted on; autoRefresh and autoRefreshTimeLimit are held, since the bridge loads nothing there is nothing to refresh; the stock body does not report isBound for the first Viewpoint at load (X_ITE does), so the test binds V1 first
Anchor.prev_note: only #Viewpoint urls are followed in the test; other urls go to body.opts.onAnchor, a page without one gets a note and stays; javascript: urls are refused on purpose; addChildren and removeChildren are accepted and not acted on; autoRefresh is not implemented; target= in parameter is passed to onAnchor, not acted on; the stock body does not report isBound for the first Viewpoint at load (X_ITE does), so the test binds V1 first

Arc2D.note: lines are not pickable, so the check is the picture (silhouette overlap and the mean colour of the drawn pixels, SwiftShader CPU raster) plus the segment count between the engines (X_ITE vertex pairs through its internal getVertices, a private API) and one line mesh in our body; line width is one pixel in both, ours is an anti-aliased ribbon
Arc2D.prev_note: lines are not pickable, so there is no hit probe: the segment count is compared between the engines (X_ITE vertex pairs via its internal getVertices, which is a private API), and our body is checked to have built one line mesh; colour and line width are not compared

ArcClose2D.note: compared by pointer-over probes, the triangle count and the picture; texture mapping and lighting of ArcClose2D are not compared with X_ITE
ArcClose2D.prev_note: compared by pointer-over probes in both engines and the triangle count; texture mapping and lighting are not compared

AudioDestination.note: mediaDeviceID would pick the output device with setSinkId; the bridge's graph ends at the page's default output with no Audio element, so it is held but not applied; the audio only plays once the page's audio context is allowed to run (a click or key on the page); this is the browser's rule, not the bridge's

BiquadFilter.note: the filter response is Web Audio's, the same engine under both; only the settings are compared; a time dependent node here only keeps the clock (isActive, isPaused, elapsedTime); the signal passes whether or not it is active, as in X_ITE

BoundedPhysicsModel.note: X_ITE 16.6.0 draws the particles white on this raster, ours uses the Material emissive colour (colour is not compared); the bounds are tested in ours from the particle list (a box of 3 x 2 x 2 holds every particle, which reflect at the faces); X_ITE's particle positions are not read, its picture is compared by extent

BufferAudioSource.note: the field is bufferLength in X_ITE 16.6.0 and bufferlength (lowercase l, output only) in the X3D 4.0 XSD and UOM; both names exist here and the test uses the X_ITE one at run time, because the XSD one cannot be written; loading from url is written (fetch and decodeAudioData, then numberOfChannels, sampleRate, bufferLength, buffer and bufferDuration are filled in) but not tested here: it needs a sound file; a pause stops the source and resume starts it again at the paused position, since a Web Audio buffer source cannot pause; autoRefresh and autoRefreshTimeLimit are held, not acted on; X_ITE 16.6.0 reports bufferDuration -1 (not the UOM's 0) from the start while load is TRUE and nothing has loaded; the bridge does the same

ChannelMerger.note: a child past the 32nd is not connected (as in X_ITE); adding or removing children at run time rebuilds the merger on the next tick

ChannelSelector.note: a disabled selector passes all channels (as in X_ITE); only the splitter size is checked, the routing of the chosen output is not read back

ChannelSplitter.note: a node past the 32nd in outputs is not connected (as in X_ITE); the wiring of each output to its node is not read back, only the splitter's size

Circle2D.note: lines are not pickable, so the check is the picture (silhouette overlap and the mean colour of the drawn pixels, SwiftShader CPU raster) plus the segment count between the engines (X_ITE vertex pairs through its internal getVertices, a private API) and one line mesh in our body; line width is one pixel in both, ours is an anti-aliased ribbon
Circle2D.prev_note: lines are not pickable, so there is no hit probe: the segment count is compared between the engines (X_ITE vertex pairs via its internal getVertices, which is a private API), and our body is checked to have built one line mesh; colour and line width are not compared

Collision.note: Library hall port (parallel port thread), 8 Nov 2026

CollisionSensor.note: needs the RigidBodyPhysics nodes it reads (CollisionCollection, CollidableShape, CollidableOffset, RigidBody, RigidBodyCollection, Contact; ranks 227 to 239) and a contact solver; a sensor with no collidables can never fire. Build them as one physics group. Scaffold kept in bridge/_deferred/

ColorChaser.note: the intermediate values are pinned against X_ITE 16.6.0 as a curve: ours runs on a virtual clock (0.05 s steps), X_ITE on the real one (frames of about 17 ms), both measured from the isActive true event; every X_ITE sample must match ours interpolated within +-0.05 s of the same elapsed time; the worst difference is relative to the largest value on the curve (at least 1) and is bounded at 0.05: ours is interpolated linearly across the kink where the red channel saturates, which is most of the difference (colour path blue to red through magenta, checked sample by sample)
ColorChaser.prev_note: hue path between start and destination not pinned against X_ITE (end state only)

ColorDamper.note: the intermediate values are pinned against X_ITE 16.6.0 as a curve: ours runs on a virtual clock (0.05 s steps), X_ITE on the real one (frames of about 17 ms), both measured from the isActive true event; every X_ITE sample must match ours interpolated within +-0.05 s of the same elapsed time (bound 0.03); X_ITE 16.6.0 never reports isActive false when the hue path crosses the 0/1 seam; the curve itself agrees (documented in xiteDisagrees)
ColorDamper.prev_note: X_ITE 16.6.0 keeps isActive true after a hue-seam path (observed 7.3 s); ours stops. Intermediate colours not pinned

ComposedTexture3D.note: XSD finding: x3d-4.0.xsd writes the texture field of a ComposedTexture3D as an xs:sequence of ImageTexture, PixelTexture, MovieTexture, ProtoInstance repeated, not an xs:choice, so the slices must come in fours in that order and two ImageTextures do not validate; the fixture is checked against the XSD with that sequence made a choice (the receipt says so); the image field of a PixelTexture3D takes decimal numbers only in the XSD (no 0x hex); Babylon side: a WGSL ShaderMaterial over a RawTexture3D, shaded by the headlight only (N dot view axis, two sided); other lights, TextureProperties anisotropy and mipmaps are not applied to volumes

Convolver.note: three channels, or more than four, are refused by Web Audio; the bridge keeps the previous response (X_ITE throws); the response is built at the audio context's own sample rate, as in X_ITE; the processed sound is not compared; numberOfChannels is a Convolver field in X_ITE 16.6.0 but is not in the X3D 4.0 UOM or XSD; the bridge has it as in X_ITE (set at run time only, since the XSD cannot write it)

CoordinateChaser.note: the intermediate values are pinned against X_ITE 16.6.0 as a curve: ours runs on a virtual clock (0.05 s steps), X_ITE on the real one (frames of about 17 ms), both measured from the isActive true event; every X_ITE sample must match ours interpolated within +-0.05 s of the same elapsed time (bound 0.02, measured 0.003): list of 2 from the initial value, grown to 3 points, shrunk to 2; a list that changes length mid-chase restarts the chase at the new length with a new tail at 0; the end state (5 5 5, 6 6 6 after a change at 0.3 s) agrees with X_ITE, the frame of the change is not pinned
CoordinateChaser.prev_note: end state only; a list that changes length mid-chase restarts at the new length with the new tail at 0 (not compared with X_ITE)

CoordinateDamper.note: the intermediate values are pinned against X_ITE 16.6.0 as a curve: ours runs on a virtual clock (0.05 s steps), X_ITE on the real one (frames of about 17 ms), both measured from the isActive true event; every X_ITE sample must match ours interpolated within +-0.05 s of the same elapsed time (bound 0.02, measured 0.007): list of 2 from the initial value, grown to 3 points, shrunk to 2; a list that changes length mid-damping restarts at the new length with a new tail at 0; the end state agrees with X_ITE, the frame of the change is not pinned
CoordinateDamper.prev_note: end state only; a list that changes length mid-chase restarts at the new length with the new tail at 0 (not compared with X_ITE)

CoordinateDouble.note: the points are kept as 32-bit floats (the geometry code reads Float32Array); doubles finer than about 7 digits or larger than 3e38 are not kept; only the triangle positions are compared with X_ITE (pointer hit and miss), not shading
CoordinateDouble.prev_note: the points are kept as 32-bit floats (the geometry code reads Float32Array); doubles finer than about 7 digits or larger than 3e38 are not kept; only the triangle positions are compared with X_ITE (pointer hit and miss), not shading

CoordinateInterpolator.note: Library hall port (parallel port thread), 8 Nov 2026

CoordinateInterpolator2D.note: Library hall port (parallel port thread), 8 Nov 2026

CylinderSensor.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 numerically: trackPoint_changed and rotation_changed in cylinder mode (off-axis press), in disk mode (axisRotation turns the axis to the view direction) and with minAngle/maxAngle; rotations compared as quaternions (X_ITE writes the same turn with the axis flipped and the angle negated); unlike X_ITE the angle accumulates past a half turn (X_ITE returns a rotation of at most 180 degrees, so a full drag around the axis jumps back); a deliberate difference, quality over match; isOver is picked once per animation frame and keeps its value while a drag is active
CylinderSensor.prev_note: disk mode (view along the axis) is implemented but only the cylinder mode is compared with X_ITE; trackPoint_changed not compared

Delay.note: Web Audio takes a maximum above 0 and below 180 s; X_ITE throws outside that, the bridge holds maxDelayTime to 0.001..179.999 (not tested, since X_ITE cannot be asked)

DirectionalLight.note: shadows and shadowIntensity are read and not used (no shadow generator is made); ambientIntensity feeds Babylon's one scene ambient colour (the sum over the lights that are on, times material ambientIntensity * diffuseColor, compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 in the picture, mad 1.6); a light with global FALSE adds its ambient to every shape, not only its group; global FALSE lights the meshes below the parent group; meshes added later are picked up when the mesh count changes (checked in our body)
DirectionalLight.prev_note: ambientIntensity is not used (no ambient term in the Babylon light); shadows are not made; global FALSE lights the meshes below the parent group; meshes added later are picked up when the mesh count changes (checked in our body, X_ITE draws the same picture)

Disk2D.note: Library hall port (parallel port thread), 8 Nov 2026

DynamicsCompressor.note: reduction is read from the audio node every tick while active; with real sound it follows the signal, here only silence is tested

ExplosionEmitter.note: particle age at the shot differs between the engines on this CPU raster (ours runs on elapsed time at about 3 frames per second under SwiftShader), so the extent is compared with a wide bound and the speed is checked from the particle list in our body; X_ITE 16.6.0 draws the particles white on this raster, ours uses the Material emissive colour (colour is not compared); the X_ITE picture also shows a swirl pattern that ours does not reproduce

Extrusion.note: Library hall port (parallel port thread), 8 Nov 2026

FillProperties.note: a shape with filled=false and hatched=false is not drawn but still answers the pointer, as in X_ITE 16.6.0 (the 4.0 text does not say); compared by pointer-over probes; the 19 hatch patterns are drawn in screen space, one texel per pixel, like X_ITE 16.6.0 (the masks are derived from its hatching images); compared in the picture with styles 3, 6, 12 and 17 (silhouette 0.96, mean abs diff 1.8 of 255 on SwiftShader); the pixel scale of a high-density screen is not read (scale 1)
FillProperties.prev_note: a shape with filled=false and hatched=false is not drawn but still answers the pointer, as in X_ITE 16.6.0 (the 4.0 text does not say); compared by pointer-over probes (hidden fill is not hit, hatched and plain fills are) and, in our body only, the hatch overlay mesh; line pattern, thickness and screen-space scaling are not compared with X_ITE; hatchStyle 7 to 19 are drawn as style 6; the pattern follows the geometry's texture coordinates, a geometry without them shows no hatch

FogCoordinate.note: only IndexedTriangleSet and the bridged geometry sets take a fogCoord; IndexedFaceSet and the others the stock reader draws do not have the field; the fog is a second copy of the mesh drawn over the first with vertex alpha = depth, so it blends after the surface is tone mapped (X_ITE blends inside the shader); vertices past the end of depth read as 0 (clear); the world Fog is new to the bridge (stock body never drew it): it fogs every mesh no LocalFog covers; all fogs share the fog law of the first active one

Gain.note: a Gain has no Web Audio node of its own beyond the input stage (as in X_ITE)

GeneratedCubeMapTexture.note: the faces of the cube are not turned like X_ITE's (flat colours cannot show it); the picture is taken from the origin of the ball in world space, not in the camera space of X_ITE's cube; the probe renders meshes as they are: it does not draw the Background spheres of other layers

ImageCubeMapTexture.note: measured against X_ITE 16.6.0 on a mirrored ball with six flat face colours (Chromium 153 SwiftShader): silhouette overlap 0.99 and mean abs diff 10.4 of 255 over the ball region (0.87 and 15.9 over the whole frame, which holds the X_ITE badge), the six face colours land at the same places (pixel probes) but our face borders are soft and curved differently from X_ITE's hard diagonal borders (Babylon samples the cube per pixel with a linear filter, X_ITE per vertex coordinate); not closed; the Material is added to the reflection, not multiplied with it; the reflection is of the world (it does not turn with the camera as CAMERASPACEREFLECTIONVECTOR does in X_ITE); flat face colours cannot show if the face images are turned like X_ITE's; a 2:1 panorama is converted but its orientation is not compared; KTX2 and DDS are not read
ImageCubeMapTexture.prev_note: the Material is added to the reflection, not multiplied with it; the reflection is of the world (it does not turn with the camera as CAMERASPACEREFLECTIONVECTOR does in X_ITE); flat face colours cannot show if the face images are turned like X_ITE's; a 2:1 panorama is converted but its orientation is not compared; KTX2 and DDS are not read

ImageTexture3D.note: the DDS volume (right) is drawn by ours and shown white by X_ITE 16.6.0 on this raster (Suspected: its DDS 3D reader does not take this uncompressed RGBA header); the picture comparison covers the NRRD volume (left); ImageTexture3D reads uncompressed DDS volumes and uchar NRRD (raw, gzip, ascii); DICOM and compressed DDS are not read

IndexedQuadSet.note: attrib is read and kept; only a shader program would consume it, and no shader language runs in the bridge (see ShaderProgram, ProgramShader)

IndexedTriangleFanSet.note: attrib is read and kept; only a shader program would consume it, and no shader language runs in the bridge (see ShaderProgram, ProgramShader)

IndexedTriangleStripSet.note: attrib is read and kept; only a shader program would consume it, and no shader language runs in the bridge (see ShaderProgram, ProgramShader)

KeySensor.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 event for event: Shift, Control and Alt flags, character keys, Enter, F1 and F12, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown and the four arrows (action codes 13-20), two keys held at once (isActive until the first release, as X_ITE), key repeat (a second keyDown raises keyPress again), enabled false; key events come from the focused canvas only (keydown and keyup, as in X_ITE); a page that keeps focus elsewhere must focus the canvas
KeySensor.prev_note: Alt/Control flags follow the Shift path but were only tested with Shift; key repeat while a key is held fires keyPress again, as in the browser

Layer.note: pickable, objectType, pointerEvents and viewport are held: picking does not respect layers; addChildren and removeChildren rebuild the layer; this is checked in the SAI test of LayerSet only if the engine exposes them (X_ITE does), here only the fields are compared

LayerSet.note: activeLayer (which layer the user navigates) and the navigation of a layer's own Viewpoint are held, not acted on: the user always navigates the world's camera; a layer's Viewpoint is read once and per frame, not bound or animated; the layer has no NavigationInfo, Background or headlight of its own; picking does not respect layers: a ray hits the meshes of every layer, and pickable / objectType / viewport are held; lights of the world light the meshes of every layer; a layer has no lights of its own; order without any visible layer draws the world (Babylon needs a camera)

Layout.note: a Layout inside a LayoutGroup that sits in the perspective world uses the near plane of the camera as the viewport size (like X_ITE); only the orthographic layer is probed here; the offset and size units of PIXEL count CSS pixels of the canvas; no device pixel ratio is read

LayoutGroup.note: viewport of a LayoutGroup is held: the world camera is shared with the rest of the scene; a LayoutGroup in the perspective world uses the near plane of the camera as the viewport size, so its layout is microscopic there, as in X_ITE; only the orthographic layer is probed; XSD finding: x3d-4.0.xsd (x3d_mcp) lists LayoutGroup only in the pick-target content model, in no child content model, so NO scene can hold a LayoutGroup and still validate; the fixture is checked against the XSD plus one line (receipt names it)

LayoutLayer.note: pickable, objectType and pointerEvents are held: picking does not respect layers; a LayoutLayer without a Layout shows its children as they are, a Layout is probed in the Layout fixture

LinePickSensor.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 in scene mode: sensors in a Transform with a Shape sibling (X_ITE 16.6.0 does not traverse a group that holds only a pick sensor, so the fixtures add a 0.02 unit Box beside each sensor); two segments through a Box and a Sphere: pickedGeometry, pickedPoint and pickedNormal compared as sets, BOUNDS and GEOMETRY; pickedPoint, pickedNormal agree within 0.02: Babylon's Sphere is tessellated differently from X_ITE's (points on the sphere differ by up to 1 percent); pickedTextureCoordinate is filled from the mesh UVs and not compared (box UV layouts differ between the engines); pickedPoint is in the target's own coordinates (as X_ITE 16.6.0)

LineSet.note: normal, fogCoord and attrib are read and ignored; line colour: the drawn pixels are about 20 percent brighter than X_ITE's one pixel lines in the picture (mean colour 60,120,61 against 48,99,51), the anti-aliased ribbon covers more pixels than a raw GL line
LineSet.prev_note: lines are not pickable, so there is no hit probe: the segment count is compared between the engines (X_ITE vertex pairs via its internal getVertices, which is a private API), and our body is checked to have built one line mesh; colour and line width are not compared; normal, fogCoord and attrib are read and ignored

ListenerPointSource.note: the listener follows the node once per frame; X_ITE does it while it draws the node; enabled = false leaves the listener where it was; interauralDistance and dopplerEnabled are held, Web Audio has no use for them; the 4.0 UOM gives ListenerPointSource gain, mediaDeviceID and a start/stop clock; X_ITE 16.6.0 has none of them, so they are held here and not compared

LoadSensor.note: Inline, audio and movie children are fetched, not decoded: loaded means the url answered; only the first working url of a child is used; X_ITE 16.6.0 hands the world over only after every resource has loaded, so the in-flight timeOut state (aborted, not yet loaded) can only be checked in our reader; the end state is compared; a change of children or enabled true restarts the count as in X_ITE 16.6.0; a child that loaded before counts at once
LoadSensor.prev_note: a change of children after load does not restart the count (X_ITE restarts); Inline, audio and movie children are fetched, not decoded: loaded means the url answered; only the first working url of a child is used; X_ITE 16.6.0 hands the world over only after every resource has loaded, so the in-flight timeOut state (aborted, not yet loaded) can only be checked in our reader; the end state is compared

LocalFog.note: EXPONENTIAL and EXPONENTIAL2 use Babylon's EXP and EXP2 scaled to 1/e at half the range: close to X3D's exp(-d/(range-d)) in the first half, softer at the end (X3D reaches full fog at the range); all LocalFogs of a world share the fog law of the first active one (Babylon picks the law per scene, not per mesh); colour and range are per scope; the range is not scaled by the parent's transform scale, X3D measures it in the LocalFog's own coordinate system; two meshes sharing one Babylon material would share the fog parameters of whichever draws first; the body makes one material per shape, so it does not happen here

Matrix3VertexAttribute.note: the matrices are attributes for a shader program; the bridge has none (WGSL ports only), so nothing is drawn from them

Matrix4VertexAttribute.note: the matrices are attributes for a shader program; the bridge has none (WGSL ports only), so nothing is drawn from them

MicrophoneSource.note: getUserMedia is not tested (no device, no permission prompt in the test browser); streamIdentifier is held; X_ITE lists it, the 4.0 UOM does not for this node

MovieTexture.note: timing is compared through the fields only; the picture on the box is not compared with X_ITE; the clip is played muted (a page may not start sound by itself); gain and pitch are read and not used; a loop and a natural end are not exercised by the test

MultiTexture.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 in the picture (silhouette 0.97, mean abs diff 1.6 of 255 on SwiftShader) for MODULATE (red x green = black) and ADD (red + green = yellow); function, source, color and alpha are read and not used; modes other than REPLACE, MODULATE, MODULATE2X, MODULATE4X and ADD are drawn as MODULATE; the combine is made once on a 256 x 256 canvas: it does not follow the lighting or the vertex colour; a small image is magnified with hard texels like X_ITE
MultiTexture.prev_note: X_ITE is compared on loading and drawing the shapes; the combined colour is checked in our body only (red x green = black for MODULATE, red + green = yellow for ADD); function, source, color and alpha are read and not used; modes other than REPLACE, MODULATE, MODULATE2X, MODULATE4X and ADD are drawn as MODULATE; the combine is made once on a 256 x 256 canvas: it does not follow the lighting or the vertex colour

MultiTextureCoordinate.note: Library hall port (parallel port thread), 8 Nov 2026

MultiTextureTransform.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 in the picture (silhouette 0.97, mean abs diff 3.2 of 255 on SwiftShader): the shifted box swaps the halves in both; only MultiTexture stages are moved; a plain TextureTransform on a single texture is applied by the Material path (bridged), not by the unlit one; edits to the transform after the build are not followed
MultiTextureTransform.prev_note: X_ITE is compared on loading and drawing the shapes; the shifted colours are checked in our body only (red|blue image shifted by half a tile swaps the halves); only MultiTexture stages are moved; a plain TextureTransform on a single texture is not applied by the stock body (TextureTransform stays 'base'); edits to the transform after the build are not followed

OrientationChaser.note: end state and bounds only (virtual time here, real time in X_ITE); curves not compared numerically

OrientationDamper.note: end state and bounds only (virtual time here, real time in X_ITE); curves not compared numerically

OrthoViewpoint.note: three pictures (default view, a wider fieldOfView, a shifted position) agree with X_ITE 16.6.0: silhouette iou 1.0 and mean difference 0.4 to 1.4 of 255 on Chromium 153.0.8010.12 SwiftShader / Babylon 9.32.0; the bound is iou 0.99, mad 3; a bind between an OrthoViewpoint and another viewpoint is a cut here (the fixture uses transitionType TELEPORT in both engines): no fly-through is drawn between a perspective and an orthographic view; the user's mouse wheel scales the area and the drag pans in view units; X_ITE's fieldOfViewOffset / fieldOfViewScale animations and viewAll are not modelled; near and far default to 0.1 and 10000 when nearDistance or farDistance is not positive (X_ITE takes the navigation avatar size for near)
OrthoViewpoint.prev_note: a bind between an OrthoViewpoint and another viewpoint is a cut: no fly-through is drawn; the user's mouse wheel scales the area, the drag pans in view units; X_ITE's fieldOfViewOffset / fieldOfViewScale animations and viewAll are not modelled; near and far default to 0.1 and 10000 when nearDistance or farDistance is not positive (X_ITE takes the navigation avatar size for near)

OscillatorSource.note: pause stops the tone (30 ms fade) and resume starts a new one, as in X_ITE; the four extra OscillatorSources are only there to hold the waves for the test

PackagedShader.note: no shader language runs: the node is only a holder (the WebGPU body runs WGSL ports of known GLSL parts); author-defined <field> declarations are not read for this node (the stock reader reads them for ComposedShader only)

PeriodicWave.note: the waveform is only used through an OscillatorSource; the type to wave-type mapping is tested there

PickableGroup.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 in scene mode: sensors in a Transform with a Shape sibling (X_ITE 16.6.0 does not traverse a group that holds only a pick sensor, so the fixtures add a 0.02 unit Box beside each sensor); pickable, objectType (ALL, NONE, one type), MATCH_ANY, MATCH_EVERY and MATCH_ONLY_ONE with one matching type, visible false; a sensor of objectType ALL sees through any group; a group of type ALL is seen by every sensor (as X_ITE 16.6.0); MATCH_EVERY and MATCH_ONLY_ONE with two matching types follow 19775-1 (every type of the sensor must be in the group, exactly one must be); X_ITE 16.6.0 counts at most one match, so those two steps run in ours only

PixelTexture3D.note: Babylon side: a WGSL ShaderMaterial over a RawTexture3D, shaded by the headlight only (N dot view axis, two sided); other lights, TextureProperties anisotropy and mipmaps are not applied to volumes

PlaneSensor.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 numerically (translation_changed, trackPoint_changed, offset, the routed box): plane drag, axisRotation 0 0 1 0.5, line mode (minPosition.x = maxPosition.x), clamp, disabled; agree within 0.1 relative on a 2 unit drag (the engines pick the press half a pixel apart); isOver is picked once per animation frame and keeps its value while a drag is active (the press owns the pointer); X_ITE does the same; line mode with both minPosition components equal turns the line along the sensor's y axis (X_ITE's first branch); translation_changed is in the sensor's own frame, as X_ITE reports it
PlaneSensor.prev_note: axisRotation is implemented (frame turned by it) but not exercised against X_ITE; trackPoint_changed is not compared: X_ITE reports it in the sensor frame, ours in the sensor frame at the press, to be checked; isOver (hover) is not raised by the drag sensors

PointLight.note: attenuation is a Babylon range cut at 1/32 of the polynomial (a0 1 0 0 means no fall-off), not X_ITE's per pixel polynomial; global=FALSE scope uses includedOnlyMeshes of the parent group; compared in our body only; ambientIntensity is not used; radius is a hard edge in X3D: Babylon has only a smooth range, so the range stays open and a mesh wholly beyond the radius is left out of the light (per mesh); a mesh that straddles the edge, like a big wall, is lit whole where X_ITE cuts a disc; checked by the colour of the spheres beyond it in both engines

PointPickSensor.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 in scene mode: sensors in a Transform with a Shape sibling (X_ITE 16.6.0 does not traverse a group that holds only a pick sensor, so the fixtures add a 0.02 unit Box beside each sensor); PointSet points inside a Box, a Sphere and a PickableGroup of another objectType; pickedPoint compared as a set (0.001), BOUNDS and GEOMETRY; pickedPoint holds the points of the PointSet in the sensor's frame, one entry per point inside a picked target (as X_ITE 16.6.0); with sortOrder CLOSEST or ANY only the reported target's points are listed

PointProperties.note: Library hall port (parallel port thread), 8 Nov 2026

Polyline2D.note: lines are not pickable, so the check is the picture (silhouette overlap and the mean colour of the drawn pixels, SwiftShader CPU raster) plus the segment count between the engines (X_ITE vertex pairs through its internal getVertices, a private API) and one line mesh in our body; line width is one pixel in both, ours is an anti-aliased ribbon
Polyline2D.prev_note: lines are not pickable: the segment count is compared between the engines (X_ITE vertex pairs via its private getVertices); colour and width are not compared

Polypoint2D.note: WebGPU has no point size: each point is a small camera-facing square drawn by a shader; X_ITE 16.6.0 draws its points much dimmer on this CPU raster (seen in the picture), colour and size are not compared; PointProperties sizing is not applied
Polypoint2D.prev_note: points cannot be picked: the point count is compared between the engines; WebGPU draws each point one pixel, X_ITE draws them with its point size; colour is not compared

PositionChaser.note: end state and bounds only (virtual time here, real time in X_ITE); curves not compared numerically

PositionChaser2D.note: end state only (virtual time here, real time in X_ITE); curves not compared numerically

PositionDamper.note: end state and bounds only (virtual time here, real time in X_ITE); curves not compared numerically

PositionDamper2D.note: end state only (virtual time here, real time in X_ITE); curves not compared numerically

PrimitivePickSensor.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 in scene mode: sensors in a Transform with a Shape sibling (X_ITE 16.6.0 does not traverse a group that holds only a pick sensor, so the fixtures add a 0.02 unit Box beside each sensor); BOUNDS and GEOMETRY (Sphere against Box where the boxes overlap and the geometries do not), sortOrder CLOSEST / ANY / ALL / ALL_SORTED, objectType filter, pickable false, enabled false; a shape outside every PickableGroup is not pickable here (as 19775-1 asks); X_ITE 16.6.0 picks it, the fixture checks it in ours only; disabling a sensor that is active raises isActive false here; X_ITE 16.6.0 keeps it true, checked in ours only; a Sphere picking geometry is a 162 point hull (0.4 percent inside the true sphere); the target is the convex hull of its mesh, so a concave target counts as its hull, as in X_ITE 16.6.0; the hull of the pickingGeometry is made when first needed and cached by geometry node, so a pickingGeometry node that is replaced is picked up on the next timestamp; non-uniform scale on the sensor is applied to the hull

ProgramShader.note: no shader language runs: the node is only a holder; ShaderProgram parts of programs are checked with the ShaderProgram node

ProtoInstance.note: ExternProtoDeclare is not loaded (external files); an instance of one is dropped with a warning; an SFNode field connected through IS to two places is copied, so a DEF inside it exists twice; IS inside a nested ProtoInstance connects values only (as fieldValue), not events; getNodeTypeName on an instance returns the type of its first inner node, not the PROTO's name; a PROTO field that is an SFNode or MFNode is not reachable through the instance's SAI object (initializeOnly values are not exposed either way in X_ITE's SAI, so the tests do not read them)

QuadSet.note: attrib is read and kept; only a shader program would consume it, and no shader language runs in the bridge (see ShaderProgram, ProgramShader)

Rectangle2D.note: Library hall port (parallel port thread), 8 Nov 2026

ScalarChaser.note: end state and bounds only (virtual time here, real time in X_ITE); curves not compared numerically

ScalarDamper.note: end state and bounds only (virtual time here, real time in X_ITE); curves not compared numerically

ScreenFontStyle.note: the node is not drawn: the Text font path of the body reads FontStyle only, and a screen font size in pixels (pointSize) is not applied; a ScreenFontStyle changes the text size with the content scale of the screen in X_ITE; none of this is reproduced

ScreenGroup.note: the pixel size comes from the depth of the group's origin only, as in X_ITE: the nearer face of a deep child looks a little larger; no snapping to whole pixels (X_ITE does not snap for ScreenGroup either); the device content scale is 1

Script.note: scripts are OFF unless the page sets R.bridge.allowScripts = true (they run code that comes with the scene); the test pages set it; shutdown(), node-valued fields, directOutput, external script files and the less common methods of the classic vector classes are not provided

ShaderProgram.note: no shader language runs: the program is a holder; the 4.0 UOM lists a sourceCode field that X_ITE 16.6.0 does not have and the XSD cannot write; it is not offered

SpatialSound.note: a SpatialSound plays only while it is drawn in X_ITE (its traversed flag, which a Switch or culling turns off); the bridge plays it whenever it is enabled; spatialize is an initializeOnly field: set at load, bypassing the panner; the routing is not read back; dopplerEnabled and priority are held; Web Audio has no doppler and there is one voice per node; a maxDistance of 0 or less is refused by Web Audio (RangeError): the old distance stays; X_ITE 16.6.0 raises the error inside its event handler, so the test does not try it

SphereSensor.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 numerically: trackPoint_changed agrees within 0.01 inside the sphere, within 0.02 where the pointer leaves the sphere (tangent plane rule) and for a press on the far half (sensor origin in front of the shape); rotation_changed: the angle agrees within 0.015 rad; after two drags the axis differs by up to 0.2 in one component: X_ITE's press hit lies about half a pixel off the pointer ray ((0.016, 0.016, 1) at the box centre, seen in its first trackPoint_changed) where ours is the pick at the pointer ((0, 0, 1)), and the composition offset * rotation amplifies it; the test bounds it at 0.25; isOver is picked once per animation frame and keeps its value while a drag is active
SphereSensor.prev_note: after the second drag the rotation angle agrees with X_ITE 16.6.0 (0.5205 vs 0.5235 rad) but one axis component differs by 0.2: the hit point of a press on an already turned box is read differently, not chased (no pixel perfection); trackPoint_changed not compared; a drag that leaves the sphere uses the nearest point of the sphere to the ray; X_ITE does the same by its own rule, only tested inside the sphere

SpotLight.note: the cone is a projection texture over tan(angle) (a Babylon SpotLight with its own exponent 0), full inside beamWidth and a linear ramp in the angle down to cutOffAngle as 19775-1 gives it; X_ITE and ours agree on the picture; two lights of the same angles share no texture (each light makes its own 256 x 256 table); attenuation and radius as on PointLight; a spot with cutOffAngle above about 88 degrees is held at 88 (a projection texture needs a cone under 180 degrees); Babylon only marks the projection of a SpotLight for update when the light's own position or direction changes, not when a parent Transform moves it: the bridge sets the (internal) dirty flag every frame; this is Likely stable on 9.32.0 but not a public API

StaticGroup.note: the static children are drawn as a Group and are not merged into one mesh as X_ITE does at load; the merge is an optimisation, it changes no field and no picture (compared below)

StreamAudioDestination.note: no network stream is made: streamIdentifier and mediaDeviceID are held

StreamAudioSource.note: no stream is read: streamIdentifier is held

StringSensor.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 step for step: typing, Backspace (also on an empty string and with deletionAllowed false), Enter, Escape, Tab, a typed string with a space, shifted letters; IME and dead-key composition are not handled by either engine: both read keydown only (X_ITE 16.6.0 KeyDeviceSensorComponent registers keydown and keyup), so a composed character arrives only if the browser also reports it as a key
StringSensor.prev_note: IME and dead-key composition are not handled (the browser reports one key at a time)

SurfaceEmitter.note: particle age at the shot differs between the engines on this CPU raster (ours runs on elapsed time at about 3 frames per second under SwiftShader), so the extent is compared with a wide bound; X_ITE 16.6.0 draws the particles white on this raster, ours uses the Material emissive colour (colour is not compared); the emission point is a random point of the surface triangles, area weighted, along the face normal (a Sphere is cut into 16 x 12 facets for this)

TexCoordChaser2D.note: end state only (virtual time here, real time in X_ITE); curves not compared numerically

TextureBackground.note: ImageTexture and PixelTexture faces are drawn and compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 by pixel probes (right and bottom faces are PixelTextures); MovieTexture faces are not drawn (a video element is not read for a background); transparency lowers the alpha of the sky and the six faces (checked in ours only); what shows through is the body's clear colour, which the stock Background node still sets from its first Background, where X_ITE shows the page behind; the sky sphere has 48 segments and a ring every 1/32 of PI plus one at every angle, so a gradient is stepped finer than the eye sees; colours are linear between rings; the sky is a sphere of radius 900 around the camera, the six faces a cube of half-size 500 inside it; scenes with a camera far clip below 900 would cut it (the body uses at least 2000)
TextureBackground.prev_note: only ImageTexture faces are drawn (the stock texture reader); PixelTexture and MovieTexture faces are not; transparency lowers the alpha of the sky and the six faces (checked in ours only); what shows through is the body's clear colour, which the stock Background node still sets from its first Background, where X_ITE shows the page behind; the sky sphere has 48 segments and a ring every 1/32 of PI plus one at every angle, so a gradient is stepped finer than the eye sees; colours are linear between rings; the sky is a sphere of radius 900 around the camera, the six faces a cube of half-size 500 inside it; scenes with a camera far clip below 900 would cut it (the body uses at least 2000)

TextureCoordinateGenerator.note: the six modes of the fixture are compared in the picture (silhouette overlap 0.98) and against the formula in our body; the CAMERASPACENORMAL and CAMERASPACEREFLECTIONVECTOR spheres differ visibly from X_ITE 16.6.0 (mean RGB difference 11 of 255 over the picture): X_ITE's own scaling of the camera-space range is not reproduced; camera-space modes are recomputed on the CPU whenever the model-view matrix changes, not in a shader; NOISE and NOISE-EYE are not made

TextureTransform3D.note: the moved strip (left) is compared by its matrix in our body only: X_ITE 16.6.0 draws it as a mostly flat colour, while its own TextureTransformMatrix3D with the same matrix (fixture TextureTransformMatrix3D) agrees with ours, so X_ITE's TextureTransform3D field handling differs from the 4.0 text (tc' = T C R S -C tc), Likely; the picture comparison covers the unmoved strip

TransformSensor.note: the official x3d-4.0.xsd cannot express TransformSensor.targetObject (containerField is limited to children, proxy, rootNode, shape, skin), so the fixture leaves it out and the test sets it through the SAI; compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 numerically (position_changed and orientation_changed within 0.001): target at the root, sensor under a translated and rotated Transform that is then moved again, target a Shape (its group's matrix), size 0 0 0 (never active) and -1 -1 -1 (always active); the sensor runs once per timestamp, so a moved target is seen one frame late
TransformSensor.prev_note: the sensor frame is its parent's; a parent that itself moves is followed through the world matrix, tested only with the root; a target that is a Shape uses its group's matrix; the official x3d-4.0.xsd cannot express TransformSensor.targetObject (containerField is limited to children, proxy, rootNode, shape, skin), so the fixture leaves it out and the test sets it through the SAI

TriangleFanSet.note: attrib is read and kept; only a shader program would consume it, and no shader language runs in the bridge (see ShaderProgram, ProgramShader)

TriangleSet2D.note: compared by pointer-over probes, the triangle count and the picture; X_ITE 16.6.0 culls the clockwise second triangle although solid is false, ours draws it facing +z (the 4.0 text: a 2D geometry has no back side), a deliberate difference
TriangleSet2D.prev_note: compared by pointer-over probes in both engines and the triangle count; the clockwise second triangle is turned to face +z in ours, X_ITE draws it two-sided

TwoSidedMaterial.note: with a light that adds ambient (ambientIntensity 0.6) and TwoSidedMaterial.ambientIntensity 1 on the sphere, our picture is brighter at the sphere's edge than X_ITE 16.6.0's (mean abs diff 4.9 of 255 against 2.5 with the default 0.2, Chromium 153 SwiftShader); ours follows 19775-1 (ambient = light ambientIntensity x material ambientIntensity x diffuseColor), X_ITE appears not to take the value (Suspected, not isolated); backAmbientIntensity is read and not compared; which side shows which colour is compared in the picture with X_ITE 16.6.0 (the lower row is turned round, so it shows the back colours; a solid=TRUE pair in the middle is culled in both engines; silhouette 0.98, mean abs diff 2.5 of 255 on SwiftShader), and in our body by pass: two meshes for solid=FALSE, one for solid=TRUE; the specular highlight of the sphere follows Phong shininess*128 and is compared in the picture
TwoSidedMaterial.prev_note: which side shows which colour is compared in the picture (the lower row is turned round, so it shows the back colours; a solid=TRUE pair in the middle is culled in both engines), and in our body by pass: two meshes for solid=FALSE, one for solid=TRUE; ambient and ambientIntensity are read and not shown (no ambient term in the headlight model); the specular highlight of the sphere follows Phong shininess*128 and is compared in the picture

ViewpointGroup.note: the proximity box is tested in the frame of the group's parent (a Transform above moves it); the test moves a group with a Transform and compares the list with X_ITE 16.6.0; retainUserOffsets is held; X_ITE 16.6.0 reads it only on the viewpoint nodes, never on a ViewpointGroup; the page decides how to show the list; the stock pages have none, so Body.viewpointList() is the only way to read it (X_ITE: getUserViewpoints)
ViewpointGroup.prev_note: the proximity box is tested in world coordinates: a ViewpointGroup under a moved Transform is tested as if the Transform were not there; retainUserOffsets is held but not applied (the stock body keeps no user offsets per viewpoint); the page decides how to show the list; the stock pages have none, so Body.viewpointList() is the only way to read it

Viewport.note: a Viewport used as a grouping node of the world builds its children but does not clip them (Babylon has one viewport per camera; the world's camera is shared); the layer's picture is squeezed into the clip rectangle, not cut out of the full picture: the same as X_ITE's viewport, which also changes the aspect

VisibilitySensor.note: occlusion by other shapes is not tested, by either engine (X_ITE 16.6.0 tests the frustum only); compared with X_ITE: inside, behind the camera, beyond the side plane, a box straddling the side plane (active), just outside (inactive), centre moved out and back, enabled false and true; one decision per frame; enterTime and exitTime are the frame timestamps
VisibilitySensor.prev_note: occlusion by other shapes is not tested (X_ITE 16.6.0 does not test it either); one decision per frame; enterTime and exitTime are the frame timestamps

VolumePickSensor.note: compared with X_ITE 16.6.0 in scene mode: sensors in a Transform with a Shape sibling (X_ITE 16.6.0 does not traverse a group that holds only a pick sensor, so the fixtures add a 0.02 unit Box beside each sensor); Cylinder and IndexedFaceSet tetrahedron as picking geometry, BOUNDS and GEOMETRY against a Box and a Sphere; picking geometries the body cannot read as vertices (anything beyond the primitives, IndexedFaceSet, IndexedTriangleSet, PointSet, line sets) never pick; the sensor stays inactive; GEOMETRY is a convex hull test (GJK); a concave picking geometry counts as its hull

WaveShaper.note: the curve is read back by length and by values, the shaping itself is Web Audio's
